subtopic: Compile time as a benchmark axis
learningObjective: Reason about when compile time should be reported alongside inference latency in benchmarks and how the choice affects fair comparison.
stem: Which statements about compile time in ML performance benchmarks are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Reporting only steady-state inference latency without disclosing compile time can hide significant real-world cost, particularly for auto-tuners (TVM Ansor, TensorRT builder tactic search) that can take minutes to hours per shape/model.

Compile time is fully amortizable in every deployment scenario: since the model is compiled once and served millions of times, per-request amortized compile time is always negligible and does not need to be reported.

For iterative research workflows (e.g., quickly iterating on model architecture), long compile times can dominate wall-clock development cost; a fair benchmark for these workflows must include compile time.
Benchmarks that compare compilers with different compile-time budgets (10 s vs 30 min) but the same inference latency should be treated as equivalent for deployment because compile is offline.

explanation: A: hiding compile time misleads readers. C: for iterative workflows compile dominates. B is too strong (there are common cases — canary deploys, autoscaling, per-tenant compile — where amortization fails). D is also wrong: even for deployment, a 30-minute compile impacts release cadence, canary strategy and rollback speed; the tradeoff is real, even if not per-request.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: canary deploys, autoscaling, per-tenant models all amortize poorly.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: compile time affects release cadence and operational agility.

assumptions: The benchmark is representative of a real workflow (development, canary, per-tenant, or steady-state).
nonImplications: Does not imply compile time must always be equal to inference; different scenarios weight them differently.
Does not imply short compile is always preferable; some workloads benefit from investing time in tuning.

distractorRationales.D: Ignores operational impact of long compiles.
